reason: All candidates are Galenic/alchemical 'inner heat'; none mentions tummo or compares traditions.
idx 0 identifies odyle with animal magnetism and idx 5 says Od boosted it; neither says Od comes from or reworks animal magnetism.
Kircher: natural magic 'took its origin from the knowledge of the sympathy and antipathy of things'.
Waite: 'the Spirits of the Air, who are the Sylphs of Paracelsian mythology'.
Guglielmini attributes innate heat to the Galenists ('the Galenists ... fabricate an innate heat').
Ojas and 'knowers of Ayurveda' sit in separate sentences; neither passage attributes ojas to Ayurveda.
The winds are joined to kindle chandali, the reverse direction; tummo is not said to produce or strengthen the winds.
Zunsheng bajian: those who seek to become immortals but lack the Great Elixirs take this compounded pill, which presupposes the elixirs make immortals.
The royal tincture called the Quinta Essentia is 'most powerful of Nature for a long life'.
Mercuriale says the elderly have diminished vigour and should exercise gently; the passage is cut before any claim that exercise restores it.
Agrippa says things receive the spirit of the world from the heavens; natural magic is not said to produce or strengthen it.
Contrasts the world's living soul with human automata only implicitly; no breath of life and no explicit opposition.
